test_policy.notes: Applicants with an academic GPA of 3.2 or higher can be admitted without ACT/SAT; those with a GPA of 3.1 or lower should submit official scores. Listed score minimums are SAT EBRW 480 and Math 440, or ACT English or Reading 17 and Math 17; the page also states a Freshman Index minimum of 2040 (500 x HSGPA + SAT EBRW + SAT Math). Required high school curriculum is 17 units (4 English, 4 math, 4 science, 3 social science, 2 foreign language). The international page does not mention ACT/SAT.

requirements.notes: Apply through the VSU application portal (apply.valdosta.edu); the Common App is not mentioned. The FAQ states a $40 application fee. International applicants send sealed official transcripts (non-U.S. coursework evaluated by a NACES member), a Certificate of Finance form (minimum $35,284 for nine months), medical form with immunization proof, a copy of passport and visa, and must buy the VSU medical insurance plan. The international page lists no minimum GPA.

deadlines.label: International application deadline (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: International page: fall April 1, spring August 1, summer February 1. Printed without a year, so fall 2027 is assumed. The freshman and FAQ pages print no domestic deadline.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required of non-native speakers. Completing Level 6 of the VSU English Language Institute (ELI) with a B or better in each class lets a student be admitted without TOEFL or IELTS if all other requirements are met; the page does not call this conditional admission. Cambridge IGCSE/O Level English 'D' or better also counts. Duolingo and SAT/ACT are not listed on the international page, although the TOEFL information page lists SAT 900 combined.

english.notes: Paper-based 523 also listed. No 1-6 band value given.
Cambridge English Scale score from B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency (Proficiency 180). Michigan English Test 55 is also accepted.

cost.notes: From the Fall 2026 fee schedule, doubled for two semesters at 15 credit hours: out-of-country tuition $10,950 per semester, mandatory fees $818 per semester ($1,636 per year, matching the CDS). Room and board is the schedule's minimum housing ($2,701, basic double room) plus the Blazer Weekly 8 meal plan ($1,658) per term; freshmen are listed on the Unlimited or 10-meal plans, so actual cost is higher. International students must buy the VSU health insurance (rate not read). The schedule estimates $33,454 for two semesters including $600 books per term

aid.notes: The international page says partial out-of-state tuition-waiver scholarships are available on a limited basis; contact the Center for International Programs. No amounts are published on the page read.
